topics.name: Archaic words to modern English (thou, thee, thy, thine)

questions.prompt: 'Thy Teacher must be great' in modern English is:
questions.rule: Thy is old English for your. Before a noun we use the possessive adjective your.

options: If Akbar heard the Ostad, he will be happy.
If Akbar hears the Ostad, he would be happy.
If Akbar heard the Ostad, he would be happy.
questions.rule: Second conditional: If + simple past, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: An infinitive is to + base verb: wanted to sing.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: First conditional: If + simple present, will + base verb: will dance.
Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing form): enjoyed listening.

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap with the modern word for 'thine'.
questions.rule: Thine = yours. A possessive pronoun stands alone without a noun, like mine.

questions.prompt: Say 'Bless us with thy song' in modern English.
questions.rule: Thy becomes your in modern English: your song.

chat: Would you go to the Himalayas to hear a great singer?
options: Yes, if I have the chance, I would go.
Yes, if I had the chance, I would go.
Yes, if I had the chance, I will go.
questions.rule: Second conditional: if I had ..., I would go. Do not mix have with would or had with will.

chat: What do you plan to do this summer?
options: I plan to learn the tabla.
I plan to learning the tabla.
questions.rule: Plan is followed by the infinitive: plan to learn.
Thine = yours. At the end, with no noun after it, use the pronoun yours.

options: Heard the Malkous Raga, the birds gathered around.
Hear the Malkous Raga, the birds gathered around.
Hearing the Malkous Raga, the birds gathered around.
questions.rule: A present participle (-ing) can open a sentence to show an action by the subject: Hearing ..., the birds.

options: Although Akbar was a king, but he dressed like a slave.
Although Akbar was a king, he dressed like a slave.
Although Akbar was a king, he dressing like a slave.
questions.rule: Although already joins the clauses, so do not add but. The main clause needs a finite verb: dressed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had + past participle: had not sung (sing, sang, sung).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After eager to, use the base verb: eager to meet.

questions.after: Akbar, I would also want to hear the Ostad.
questions.rule: For an imaginary situation, use If I were ..., I would ....
Two actions by the same subject are joined by and to make a compound sentence.
Adjective + infinitive: eager to perform.

chat: Why did Akbar dress like a poor man?
options: He dressed like that because of the Ostad never sang for kings.
He dressed like that because the Ostad never sang for kings.
He dressed like that because the Ostad never sing for kings.
questions.rule: because + clause (because of + noun only). The Ostad is singular, so sang, not sing.

questions.source: If you do not practise daily, you will not sing well.
options: Unless you do not practise daily, you will not sing well.
Unless you practise daily, you will not sing well.
Unless you practise daily, you would not sing well.
questions.rule: Unless means if not, so drop the not from that clause and keep will.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After a preposition use -ing (of singing); after to use the base verb (to sing); started burning.

questions.prompt: 'Thou art my teacher' in modern English is:
questions.rule: Thou art is old English for you are. You always takes are.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The birds and beasts is plural, so the finite verb is gather. Enchanted is a past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Third conditional result: would have + past participle: would never have heard.
The birds were charmed by the raga (passive meaning), so use the past participle charmed.

questions.before: Not only did Tansen sing well,
questions.rule: The pair is not only ... but also.
Third conditional: If + hadn't + past participle, then would have + past participle: would have burnt.

chat: Do you know what 'Whither goest thou?' means?
questions.rule: A wh- question puts the helping verb before the subject: Where are you going?

chat: What would you have done if you had been Akbar?
options: I would have went to the cave too.
I will have gone to the cave too.
I would have gone to the cave too.
questions.rule: Third conditional answer: would have + past participle: would have gone.

questions.prompt: Make it a complex sentence using 'when'.
questions.source: Hearing the song, Akbar fell into a trance.
options: When Akbar heard the song, and he fell into a trance.
When Akbar heard the song, he fell into a trance.
When Akbar hears the song, he fell into a trance.
questions.rule: A complex sentence has one main clause and a when clause; don't add and, and keep both verbs in the past.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: would have + past participle: come. A request with please uses the base verb: please tell me.

options: The raga singing by the Ostad filled the cave with peace.
The raga sang by the Ostad filled the cave with peace.
The raga sung by the Ostad filled the cave with peace.
questions.rule: The raga was sung (passive meaning), so use the past participle sung: the raga sung by the Ostad.

options: Had Akbar not travelled, he would have missed the song.
Had Akbar not travelled, he would missed the song.
Had Akbar not travel, he would have missed the song.
questions.rule: Had + subject + past participle can replace If; the result is would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For things like a cave, the relative pronoun is which (or that), not who.

questions.prompt: 'Thou knowest the answer' in modern English:
questions.rule: Thou knowest = you know. With you the present verb has no -s.

questions.prompt: Make a complex sentence that shows purpose.
questions.rule: so that + would introduces a clause of purpose in the past.

chat: Why did you stop going to music class?
options: I stopped going because I wanted preparing for exams.
I stopped going because I wanted to prepare for exams.
I stopped go because I wanted to prepare for exams.
questions.rule: Stop + gerund (stopped going); want + infinitive (wanted to prepare).

chat: How was the concert last night?
options: Not only was the singing good, but the tabla player were also great.
Not only was the singing good, but the tabla player was also great.
Not only was the singing good, and the tabla player was also great.
questions.rule: When Not only begins a clause, invert the verb (was the singing) and pair it with but also; the tabla player is singular.

questions.prompt: Make it a simple sentence using 'Having'.
questions.source: The Ostad finished his song and vanished.
options: Having finished his song, the Ostad vanished.
Having finish his song, the Ostad vanished.
Having finished his song, the Ostad vanish.
questions.rule: Having + past participle shows the first action; the sentence keeps one finite verb: vanished.

questions.prompt: Combine as one mixed conditional sentence using 'if'.
questions.source: Riya did not practise yesterday. She is nervous now.
options: If Riya had practised yesterday, she would not be nervous now.
If Riya practised yesterday, she would not be nervous now.
If Riya had practised yesterday, she would not have been nervous now.
questions.rule: Mixed conditional: past condition (had practised) with a present result (would not be ... now).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: agree to + base verb (agreed to go); after the preposition of use a gerund (tired of walking).

options: If the maiden would not have sung Malhar, Tansen might have died.
If the maiden had not sung Malhar, Tansen might have died.
If the maiden had not sung Malhar, Tansen might have die.
questions.rule: Never put would in the if clause. Third conditional: had not sung ..., might have died.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The pair is hardly ... when (but no sooner ... than).

questions.after: the long road, Akbar finally reached the holy cave.
questions.rule: A perfect participle (Having + past participle) shows an action completed before the main action.
Although starts the subordinate clause; the main clause follows the comma, without but.

chat: How would you say 'Mighty thy Teacher must be' in modern English?
options: I would say 'Your teacher must is mighty.'
I would say 'You teacher must be mighty.'
I would say 'Your teacher must be mighty.'
questions.rule: Thy becomes your, and a modal like must is followed by the base verb be.

questions.source: To thee I sing; he sings to God.
options: I sing to thou; he sings to God.
I sing to your; he sings to God.
I sing to you; he sings to God.
questions.rule: Thee is the old object form; after the preposition to, modern English uses you.

questions.source: Won by their humility, the Ostad sang for them.
options: The Ostad was won by their humility, and he sung for them.
The Ostad was won by their humility, and he sang for them.
The Ostad was winning by their humility, and he sang for them.
questions.rule: A compound sentence joins two main clauses with and; was won by is passive, and the past of sing is sang.

questions.prompt: Rewrite as a third conditional sentence.
questions.source: Akbar was humble, so the Ostad sang for him.
options: If Akbar was not humble, the Ostad would not have sung for him.
If Akbar had not been humble, the Ostad would not have sang for him.
If Akbar had not been humble, the Ostad would not have sung for him.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had not been ..., would not have + past participle sung (not sang).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: No sooner ... than; Each of takes a singular verb (was); the story is past, so sat.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Like thee/thy, modern pronouns change form: object him after gave, possessive his before a noun.
